artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Woodham complained that South Florida Presbytery erred by excommunicating a Teaching Elder it had previously deposed without first assigning him to membership in a particular church as required by BCO 46-8. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that Presbytery retained jurisdiction over a deposed minister until transfer to a local church was completed, and that Presbytery's efforts to implement BCO 46-8 showed no clear error; two concurring opinions (RE Donahoe and RE Eggert) offered alternative reasoning regarding the scope of Presbytery's residual jurisdiction.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley erred in approving a Session's erasure of a member's name from the roll under BCO 38-4 after she pled not guilty to a charge of failing to submit to church government and pursued divorce contrary to the Session's counsel. The SJC found multiple constitutional errors including improper conflation of a not-guilty plea with refusal to submit, failure to consider whether the member would fulfill vows in another branch of the church, failure to notify the member of her erasure, and proceeding to a case without process after dropping formal charges.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that Anna Lewis's BCO 40-5 report filed directly with the SJC was out of order, holding that the SJC's only responsibility under Chapter 40 arises upon referral from the General Assembly per RAO 16-10.c. Six members dissented, arguing the SJC has historically exercised direct jurisdiction over BCO 40-5 reports and that the majority's interpretation was overly narrow and a departure from settled precedent.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC largely denied TE Abshire's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, finding that the Presbytery did not err in appointing a judicial commission or issuing a pastoral exhortation, but sustained the error in the commission's ruling on Lynch and Rooney's complaint without following BCO 43 procedures, remanding that specific matter to Presbytery.
